identity: Utrecht University BSc Economics and Business Economics, English, three years

sources.scope: Current student timetable, context and macro choices, and year-three options.
Official prospective curriculum, subject content and programme identity.
Flexible Economics, Public Economics, Finance and Management elective groupings.
Optional course profile choices and two advanced courses in a self-composed profile.
Adopted EER Articles 3.4–3.6a and 7.4, and Annex 1.
Graduation checklist for cohorts from 2022 without a dedicated minor.

curriculum: The 180 EC degree without a dedicated minor consists of 135 EC of major study and 45 EC of open profiling. The major contains 75 EC of prescribed work, a 7.5 EC context choice, a 7.5 EC intermediate macroeconomics choice, 22.5 EC of major electives including at least one at level 3, a 7.5 EC advanced research elective and a 15 EC applied economics thesis course. The introduction, Strategy and Organisation and the historical context course supply the 22.5 EC context requirement. The student timetable shows five possible major elective slots, but the regulations and graduation checklist require three ordinary major electives and one research elective. To display a complete 60 EC per year and all six open choices, period 4 of year two remains open, while year three retains the first-listed Economics group: Labour Economics, Causes and Consequences of Inequality and Development and Growth. Study routes are flexible course groupings. The comparator does not represent an officially prescribed sequence of these particular electives.
progression: The 2026–27 EER sets a 45 EC first-year binding advice threshold subject to the specified exceptions. The self-composed open profile contains at least 15 EC intermediate by the EER and two level 3 courses by the graduation checklist. The three named advanced electives and thesis give 37.5 EC advanced in the major. The profile supplies a further 15 EC advanced, and overlapping choices can lose credit. For period 4, ECB3OKVECO requires at least 90 EC at the start of the academic year, then a pass in Econometrics, two level 3 courses including at least one in economics, and the skills reflection report before the course starts. The course assessment is participation and presentation (20%) and an individual research paper (80%).
